meta_title: GrubMarket AI Alternative for Distributors in 2026
meta_desc: GrubAssist hands your team a voice assistant. This GrubMarket AI alternative hands your customers the app, so your team never builds the order.
text: Won back on each order that leaves the phone
Is all most distributors wait to go live
Is when an account can send one
Why teams want an alternative to GrubMarket AI

GrubMarket AI calls GrubAssist a virtual assistant for the food supply chain, and the jobs it advertises are business analysis, performance, cash flow and spotting anomalies, with order creation among them. All useful. None of it stops your customer sending a message for somebody to interpret, which is where a GrubMarket AI competitor usually gets raised.
The microphone is pointed the wrong way

An assistant your staff talk to still means your staff are the ones entering the order. Faster entry is better than slow entry, but it is not the same as the order arriving already built by the person who wanted it.
There is a model to tailor
They ship a training module precisely because an assistant has to be taught your business. That is honest engineering, and it is also a project with an owner, a backlog and a before-and-after.
A product set when you needed one
An assistant, order extraction, chatbots, market pricing data. Buying the piece you actually want can mean sitting through a demo of three you do not, and then deciding which ones you are paying for.
What a GrubMarket AI alternative does from the other side
The kitchen talks, and your desk reads

A chef counts what is low and says it into their own phone. Each item comes up as a line with a quantity, they correct anything wrong, and they send it. That is the whole exchange, and your team is not in it.
Nothing arrives that the buyer has not looked at
From a walk-in or a bench, whenever the shift ends
20 to 30 minutes back against the same order by phone
Interrupted halfway? It holds the order until they come back
Your lists are the only setup there is
Nothing gets taught here. You send the lists you already keep per customer, we load them against your SKUs at the prices you hold for that account, and the configuration is finished.
A kitchen sees nothing but the lines it buys
Pricing and the catalog remain yours to set
Change a list once and it stands on the orders after
No tuning as volumes or categories grow
Delivered in whatever shape you asked for
A finished order leaves as an email carrying a PDF, Excel or Word file, or goes straight into your ERP over the API, over EDI, or into QuickBooks, in a shape your desk opens daily.
Addressed to a rep, or to the purchasing desk
On a direct feed there is no rekeying at your end
Picking, billing and delivery carry on unchanged
No part of your stack has to be retired first
What is on hand, as the orders come in

VOS carries real-time inventory visibility tied to what is being ordered, and the catalog updates as stock levels change. It is not the system of record for stock: yours stays in charge, and a demo shows how the levels connect.
Every line you carry, not only the quick movers
Fewer stockout surprises on a late, heavy order
Numbers come out of whatever you count with now
When VOS and GrubMarket AI work together
VOS is not a GrubMarket AI replacement and does not try to be. It adds on, so an assistant the team already leans on is no reason to leave this alone.
Keep the assistant for the questions
Asking out loud how a customer is trending, or where the cash is, is a genuinely useful thing and VOS cannot do it. Those questions keep their home, and the order stops being one of them.
Shrink the pile that needs extracting

Each account you move across sends a structured, approved order rather than a voicemail. Whatever is doing the extracting has less to work through, and the hardest messages are the ones that leave first.
One place for it to land, whatever else you run
Whatever you add, the order still lands in the one system you chose, over EDI, the API or QuickBooks, so nobody ends up with two places to look.
See an order arrive already finished
Twenty minutes. A buyer speaks an order, approves it, and it arrives on the desk as a PDF, over EDI or over the API.
Three steps, and no model to teach
Nothing has to be trained and no pilot has to be designed. You send lists, we open accounts, your customers order.
Whatever format they are already in. Each account's lines and your prices go into a single admin screen, lined up with your codes.
Accounts get created and the kitchen gets shown the app. Most send something in before the day is out.
Signed off by the buyer, carrying a number and a time, in the shape your system expects.

VOS puts the app in your customers' hands. GrubAssist is an assistant for your own staff that can also build an order, which is the distinction that matters when a GrubMarket AI alternative comes up. Both products use it, so the rows below mark whose hands it is in.
An app your customers speak the order into
Your buyer signs the order off before it sends
Answers questions about your business by voice
Each account has its own list, at your prices
Pulls orders out of voicemails, emails and texts
Order number and the time it was sent
Something to train or tailor first
How long until it is running
What changes on your order desk
What gets asked when two voice tools go head to head
Is VOS a real GrubMarket AI alternative, and is it better than GrubMarket AI?

They use the same technology at opposite ends. GrubAssist is for your staff: ask it about the business, have it write up an order. VOS is for your customers: they speak it and approve it, so your staff never build one. For getting an order in without anyone on your side building it, we think VOS is better, because the buyer does the work and signs it off. For asking your data questions out loud, no, and not by a little: VOS does not do that at all.
Can VOS tell us how a customer is performing?

No. You can see what an account has ordered, and that is the extent of it. Business analysis, cash flow, anomaly spotting: all of that is on their list and none of it is on ours. Worth knowing before you shortlist us against them.
Do we have to teach VOS our catalog?

No, and there is no module for it, because nothing has to be taught. The item list you keep for an account is the configuration. Load it, and spoken items land on the right rows at the price you hold.
Does any of this touch our ERP?

Only to hand it the order. It never goes near your ERP beyond handing in what the buyer approved. GrubAssist connects to an ERP so it can answer questions about the business; VOS only ever delivers into one. Everything downstream behaves exactly as it did yesterday.

Neither of us publishes a figure. Ours arrives as a quote once we know your setup. Theirs comes after a demo. With that much on their side, the thing to pin down is which ones the quote actually covers.
How soon could our accounts be ordering?

For most distributors this is live inside 24 to 48 hours, and most kitchens place one the same day. There is no training phase, which is the bulk of the difference. They publish no timeline, so ask them for one rather than take a number from us.
And the accounts that will only ever call?

They carry on telephoning, and your desk deals with those the way it always has. Be clear about the limit though: a call or a voicemail gets no order number from VOS, no timestamp and nothing moving in stock. Only what comes through the app does.
Where do the GrubMarket details on this page come from?

Taken from grubmarket.ai on 10 October 2026, which is the GrubMarket AI product rather than GrubMarket the company: the GrubAssist description, the list of advertised jobs, the training module and the other products all come off that page. They publish no price and no rollout time, so this page does not guess at either. If any of it has moved on, the fault is here, not there.
